family.tagline: Two studies, two small businesses and one Companion Core.
family.story: Ingrid runs an events consultancy from the study beside the front door, where the Companion Core sits. Mats writes backend code for his own clients in the study upstairs. One Core holds the files, code and hours of both businesses.

companion.name: Rosemary
companion.job: Opens Twenty in its own browser and edits the deals Ingrid lists.
companion.limits: Edits deals only. Ingrid checks every field before it stands.

companion.name: Thyme
companion.job: Opens Kimai in its own browser and enters the hours Mats lists.
companion.limits: Enters hours only. Mats reads every line before he invoices.

popup.title: Mats carries the parcel in
popup.body: A parcel waits by the front door. Mats carries it in while Ingrid clears her desk for the Companion Core.

popup.title: Ingrid lifts out the Core
popup.body: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Ingrid sets the Core on her desk, in sight of the door.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: Mats plugs in the cable, and Ingrid presses the button. The Companion Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Ingrid joins from her phone
popup.body: On her phone, Ingrid opens the Wi-Fi settings and joins the Core’s own network. Then she chooses the home network.

popup.title: Two agents get their names
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Ingrid and Mats pick OpenClaw, and Ingrid approves its link to Companion Memory. The family names the agents Rosemary and Thyme.

beats.capability: an agent with browser automation and tool use, running in a sandboxed app on your Core

popup.title: Rosemary says hello
popup.body: Ingrid greets Rosemary, the agent the family named. Rosemary answers from the Core on Ingrid’s desk.

say.speaker: ingrid
say.text: I am Rosemary. What comes first today?

beats.capability: keep customers, deals and custom fields in a CRM you host yourself

popup.title: A walkthrough changes the deal
popup.body: The venue walkthrough moves a client’s date and headcount. Ingrid lists the changes. Rosemary edits the deal in Twenty on the Core, and Ingrid checks each field before it stands.

beats.capability: plan tasks and time blocks in one local file on your Core

popup.title: Ingrid picks which client goes first
popup.body: Two clients want the same Saturday. Ingrid gives the morning to the first walkthrough. Companion Planning holds the second client’s follow-ups, in one local file on the Core.

beats.capability: merge, split, compress and convert PDFs on your own Core

popup.title: The venue wants one file
popup.body: The venue manager asks for one file. Ingrid merges the run sheet, floor plan and supplier list in Stirling-PDF on her Core. Then she prints a copy.

beats.capability: keep customers, deals and custom fields in a CRM you host yourself

popup.title: Ingrid files the anniversary guest list
popup.body: The anniversary guest list holds names, addresses and seating notes. Ingrid keeps it in Twenty, on the Core, where a hosted CRM would have held it.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping and meals

popup.title: The week fits on one calendar
popup.body: Sunday morning on the sofa, Ingrid and Mats put her site visits and his client calls into one Yuvomi calendar. The calendar lives in a database on the Core.

beats.capability: control and automate your smart home from one place, locally, without a cloud account

popup.title: Mats gives the lamps a scene
popup.body: Saturday afternoon, Mats picks one Home Assistant scene before the film, and the pendant lamps by the TV dim. Home Assistant runs it from the Core, with no cloud account.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping and meals

popup.title: Wednesday’s dinner needs dill
popup.body: The herb pots hold rosemary and thyme but no dill. Mats, cooking on Wednesday, adds it to the shared Yuvomi list, and Ingrid adds lemons from her study.

beats.capability: split shared costs and settle up with the fewest payments

popup.title: Ingrid settles the crew lunch
popup.body: Back home after set-up day, Ingrid enters the crew lunch in Spliit at the breakfast bar. It works out the fewest payments to settle up.

beats.capability: host your own Git repositories, issues and pull requests on your Core

popup.title: A fix goes up before lunch
popup.body: A bug fix is ready before lunch, so Mats pushes it to Forgejo. The repository and its issues sit on the Core, not on a rented code host.

beats.capability: write and run notebooks, code and data in a browser, on your Core

popup.title: Mats asks about a failing test
popup.body: A test fails and Mats cannot see why. He reruns it in JupyterLab, then asks a model on the Core through Open WebUI. The chat stays there by default.

beats.capability: host your own Git repositories, issues and pull requests on your Core

popup.title: A request comes up the stairs
popup.body: Ingrid calls up the stairs that her seating plans should print on one sheet. Mats opens an issue in Forgejo, and it waits on the Core beside the code.

beats.capability: track time per project and client, with reports

popup.title: Monday starts with a timer
popup.body: Monday morning, Mats starts a Kimai timer before the first ticket. His hours are grouped by client, so the report is ready when he writes the invoice.

beats.capability: track time per project and client, with reports

popup.title: Thyme fills in the forgotten hours
popup.body: On Thursday Mats forgets the timer. He lists the afternoon’s tasks, and Thyme opens Kimai in its own browser and enters the hours. Mats reads them before he invoices.

say.speaker: mats
say.text: The hours are entered. Please read every line.

beats.capability: control and automate your smart home from one place, locally, without a cloud account

popup.title: The planters get a morning timer
popup.body: Beside the front door, a Wi-Fi plug now powers the planters’ drip pump. Ingrid sets a seven o’clock start, and Home Assistant runs it from the Core.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping and meals

popup.title: Pool day goes on the board
popup.body: Pool day is Saturday, and skimming is the first card on the shared Yuvomi board. Mats ticks it off once the water is clear.

popup.title: One Core serves both studies
popup.body: Ingrid works below and Mats above, and both studies share one Companion Core.

closing.body: Two studies, two businesses and one household can share a Companion Core at home. Start in the Companion Hub store.

notes: The ground-floor Study has no desk item in the spec: the Core stands on its own desk there. Ingrid's beats anchor on the core, the bookshelf and the room; Mats's use the writing desk and the dual-monitor arm upstairs.
up-model uses JupyterLab as the beat app with Open WebUI in with: the Open WebUI replaces ChatGPT chip trips cap-parity. No cloud key is mentioned; the model is the one on the Core.
Both agents are OpenClaw and work only in Twenty and Kimai, apps on the Core with a web interface; no beat opens an outside website, so the OpenClaw website note is not carried.
garden-plants assumes a Wi-Fi plug on a drip line for the forecourt planters; it is not in the 3D scene. Home Assistant is network devices only, no Zigbee stick.
Sleeping is never told. Nobody is shown asleep and no beat frames the bed.
